prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer looks straight down at their own torso (brightest white at the bottom, roughly 0.1–0.3 m from the head-mounted camera) and outstretched arms reaching down to a raised rectangular metal work surface at mid-grey depth (about 0.5–0.7 m below the camera), while the workshop floor and stacked vertical panels on the left sit further below in dark grey to black (about 1.0–1.5 m away). No other people are present; the wearer faces forward toward the metal panel edge with their chest and stomach occluding the floor directly underneath them, and both hands remain in contact with the panel within immediate arm's reach (0.4–0.6 m from the camera, spaced roughly 0.05–0.25 m apart from each other). Across the five frames, the wearer's hands converge at the panel corner in frame 2, align along the near edge in frames 3–4 (where the wearer's feet briefly appear at around 1.2 m below), and shift downward in the frame in frame 5 as the camera tilts forward to expose more of the tabletop ahead. Compared to the RGB strip, where specular highlights on the polished stainless steel and cluttered floor cables make vertical elevation hard to judge, the depth map clearly separates the three height tiers of body, worktable, and floor. However, the depth map is unreliable around the hands on the reflective metal surface, where the fingers blend into the tabletop depth and lose crisp boundary definition, and in frame 5 where torn protective film on the flat metal creates faint false depth variations.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's foreground torso and arms (roughly 0.1–0.6 m from the camera and within arm's reach) against an unlabelled black background, with no other people in the scene and the wearer's body oriented downward toward the top of the frame while occluding the floor below. Across the five frames, the foreground masks track the wearer's arms moving from separated positions (about 0.25 m apart in frame 1) to joined at the centre (frame 2), parallel in front of the torso (frames 3–4), and shifted toward the lower-right in frame 5 as the camera tilts forward. While the masks help separate the wearer's body contour from the cluttered workshop floor in frames 2–4, the map provides almost no scene layout or object understanding because it completely misses the primary stainless-steel panel (0.5–0.7 m away), handheld tools, and floor equipment (~1.2 m away). Furthermore, the segmentation is highly unreliable: it fragments the single camera wearer into multiple overlapping or separate `person` instances (splitting the left arm in frame 1 and separating the torso and right arm into cyan and pink masks in frame 5), merges the gap between the arms into a solid pink blob in frames 2–4, and hallucinates false `book` (frame 1, upper left at ~1.0 m) and `laptop` (frame 2, middle right at ~0.8 m) labels on background workshop materials.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely black and detects only a single magenta left-hand skeleton in frames 2, 3, and 4 at roughly 0.4–0.5 m in front of and below the camera wearer, positioned just left of the midline within immediate arm's reach. In those middle frames, the 3D-projected finger keypoints show the left hand curled into a pinching posture oriented toward the metal panel edge, shifting slightly upward and leftward from the central corner in frame 2 to the horizontal edge in frames 3 and 4. This skeletal wireframe reveals the exact articulation of the curled left fingers in frames 2–4, which are dark and self-occluded against the shadowed metal seam in the RGB image. However, the map is largely unreliable for broader spatial understanding because the extreme top-down egocentric perspective and self-occlusion of the head and shoulders cause complete omission of the yellow body skeleton across all five frames, total failure to detect the right hand (located 0.05–0.25 m to the right of the left hand), and complete omission of the left hand in frames 1 and 5 despite both hands being clearly visible in the RGB strip.
